When there’s a monopoly on something required to function (Internet has gotten there), companies should not be able to do whatever the fuck they want.

The internet exploded in the US because anyone could start an ISP, and the phone company (who had a monopoly) had to let you call their number. The phone company couldn’t charge you more for calling modems than non-modems, and they couldn’t stop people from making things compatible with phone lines.

Some countries split ISPs into two categories - dumb pipes (who have government monopolies, being one of 1 or 2 options to get to your houses), and ISPs (like the old ISPs). Dumb pipes have to sell wholesale, and have no say in what people do with it. Regular ISPs can all use those lines (like the ISPs with the phone company), and can filter, censor, prioritize, etc. as they see fit. If you don’t like it, you have lots and lots of options for other ISPs that won’t.

When you need a phone and internet to work, or insulin to live, or you’re in an ambulance and are being taken to the nearest hospital, it’s not a market. We should quit pretending it is. Let the market do what it’s good at, and regulate when it’s not.
